lesson.title: Honger, Dorst & Leeftijd
lesson.subtitle: Dutch says you 'have' hunger and thirst — but you 'are' your age

hook.title: Have Hunger, Be Age
hook.content: Dutch says ik heb honger and ik heb dorst, not 'I am hungry/thirsty'. But age uses zijn: ik ben twintig jaar. Two body states, two different verbs.

pattern.title: Have states, be age
pattern.content: Ik heb honger, ik heb dorst, wij hebben geen honger. Age: ik ben twintig jaar. The noun is possessed; the age is predicated.
pattern.trap_note: Never say ik heb twintig jaar for age, and never say ik ben honger for hunger.

exercises.prompt: Match each English meaning with its Dutch twin (Honger, Dorst & Leeftijd):
exercises.target_answer: de honger, de dorst, het jaar, twintig, hebben, zijn
exercises.meaning: hunger, thirst, year, twenty, to have, to be
exercises.explanation: These are the anchors of "Honger, Dorst & Leeftijd": read each Dutch form through the pattern, not as a new word.
“Ik heb honger.” is the Dutch form; the other readings bend the pattern of “Honger, Dorst & Leeftijd”.

cues: The pattern: Have states, be age
exercises.explanation: “Ik heb dorst.” puts the thought together the Dutch way — Have states, be age.

diagnosis.slip: an English-shaped word order slipped in
diagnosis.cue: Never say ik heb twintig jaar for age, and never say ik ben honger for hunger.

exercises.prompt: Which English sentence is built the Dutch way?
exercises.explanation: “Ik ben twintig jaar.” is word-for-word “I am twenty year.”. The odd English is the lesson — never a model to produce. Pattern: Have states, be age.

exercises.prompt: Listen and write the whole sentence.
cues: It means: We are not hungry.
exercises.explanation: “Wij hebben geen honger.” reuses only material taught in “Honger, Dorst & Leeftijd” — Have states, be age.
exercises.affirmation: You heard “Wij hebben geen honger.” — a sentence built from the lesson's own Dutch, practising Have states, be age.

twist.prompt: One more, no safety net — say: “I feel like eating.”
twist.explanation: Trek is the appetite word; it takes hebben like honger.

summary.outcome: Say hunger, thirst and age with the correct verb.
summary.takeaway: Dutch divides bodily states and age between hebben and zijn; the noun decides.
summary.curiosity_teaser: Up next on De Brug: Koffie, Brood & De Rekening.

honger.etymology_derivation: English hunger and Dutch honger are the same word; Dutch says 'have hunger'.

dorst.etymology_derivation: English thirst and Dutch dorst are the same word; Dutch says 'have thirst'.

jaar.etymology_derivation: English year and Dutch jaar are the same word; both take a y/j, not a g.

twintig.etymology_derivation: English twenty and Dutch twintig are the same word; age uses zijn.

hebben.etymology_derivation: English have and Dutch hebben descend from the same verb; the b is preserved.

zijn.etymology_derivation: The being verb is irregular in every Germanic language; English is and Dutch is are the same old root.
